blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (A dropped webhook is only logged at debug level, and a non-2xx response is not logged at all) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: When a merchant's endpoint answers 500 five times, the loop falls through without any log for those attempts (only thrown errors are logged), and the final give-up is a `console.debug` line, filtered out in production: the payment event is permanently lost and no operator can see it or tell the merchant. Use the project's structured `logger` (as `src/events.ts` does): log each failed attempt with fields (`eventId`, `attempt`, `status` or `error`, merchant id or host, never the full URL if it can carry a secret), and log the drop with `logger.error` so it can be alerted on; consider a counter of dropped deliveries.
findings.title: A dropped webhook is only logged at debug level, and a non-2xx response is not logged at all

findings.recommendation: The retries are bounded and idempotent (`x-event-id`), but not spaced: when a merchant's server returns 503 or refuses connections during a restart, the five attempts fire back to back within milliseconds, hammering an endpoint that is already struggling and exhausting every attempt inside a few-second outage, so the event is dropped (see R-ops-1). Wait between attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s), ideally from a queue or scheduled job rather than an in-process sleep (see R-ops-3).
findings.title: Failed deliveries are retried immediately, with no backoff

findings.recommendation: `publish` in `src/events.ts`, called by the payment service once a payment is settled, awaits each listener in turn. When a merchant's endpoint hangs, `deliver` holds that `publish` call for up to five 5-second timeouts (25s, more once backoff is added), delaying every listener registered after it and the payment service's own flow; a slow merchant becomes an incident on the payment path. Enqueue the delivery (outbox table or job queue) and return from the listener immediately, or at least do not await `deliver` there, catching and logging its outcome.
findings.title: Webhook delivery runs inline in the payment event listener and blocks `publish`
